_: Per-room AUTHORED OBJECT placement -- every kind the set files classify, not just the boxes. Answers psz-godot #578 and the 43%-invisible follow-up. Generated by tools/objplace.py; do not hand-edit.
FOR_THE_CONSUMER: THE LIST KEY IS STILL `boxes`. It is a historical name and it now holds EVERY emitted kind, so an importer that already reads per_room[*].boxes picks the new kinds up with no code change. Key off `kind`.

SCHEMA, unchanged: each entry is {group, kind, x, y, z, angle} plus `model`, `slot`, `factory_index`, `variant`, `registry` for reference. x/y/z are ROOM-LOCAL, same frame as data/room_doorways.json; angle is the u16 facing at record +0x10.

KIND NAMES are the game's own model stem (o0c_key, o0c_fence, o0c_trebox, o0s_warpm, ...) for everything except the container family, which keeps the generic `box`, `wall` and `rare_box` because its model is stage-specific. The stem is single-valued for every (factory index, variant) the corpus uses, so the name is a fact about the ROM and not an interpretation.

THE EIGHT TRAPS ARE NOT HERE. They are in data/trap_placement_per_room.json and are DECLINED here as `in_the_trap_dump`, so merging both files places each trap exactly once. Do not change that without changing both files.

THERE IS A SECOND LIST NOW: `volumes`, and it is ADDITIVE -- `boxes` is byte-for-byte what it was, so an importer that only reads `boxes` is unaffected. `volumes` holds the SIX MODELLESS mechanisms that used to be declined as `unresolved_factory_index`: player_entry, town_service, mayors_office, event_trigger_volume, field_scene_effect, ambient_sound. None of them has a model -- placing one as a model would place nothing -- so each entry carries {group, kind, x, y, z, angle, slot, factory_index} plus the fields its own constructor reads out of its parameter block. See `volumes_rule` for what each one does.

EVERY ROOM RECONCILES: accounting.emitted + accounting.emitted_volumes + sum(accounting.declined) == sum(group_sizes). If it ever does not, the dump is lying and the generator says so rather than dropping the record.

the_rule.1_the_positions_are_authored: set/<NN>/<v>/<room>/<stage><v>_<room>_<set>.rel, 24-byte records, room-local x/y/z in 1.19.12 plus a u16 facing at +0x10. NOTHING is scattered at runtime.
the_rule.2_which_file: the set family is ONE byte per session -- u8 at *(0x0211A3C4)+0x0C, 0=d 1=s 2=f<n> -- see data/object_set_selector.json
the_rule.3_which_groups_of_it_get_built: a set file is SIX groups. FUN_02031164 picks ONE of five layout masks at 0x020EC288 = [0x21,0x23,0x25,0x28,0x30] = [[0,5],[0,1,5],[0,2,5],[3,5],[4,5]], indexed by the generated room record's byte at +0x31. A mask is eligible only if every group it names is non-empty (group 5's bit is forced in with |0x20). If +0x31 is not eligible the highest eligible index at or below 3 wins, else 0.
the_rule.3b_WHAT_FORCES_LAYOUT_4: layout 4 (mask 0x30 = groups 4 and 5) is NOT reachable from +0x31 -- FUN_02082814 draws 0..3 -- and FUN_02031164 forces it from the SESSION instead, BEFORE it ever looks at the room record. It returns 4 when all three hold: FUN_02084BF8(0x0211A51C) is non-zero, FUN_02084C4C(0x0211A51C) is zero, and mask 4 is eligible (group 4 non-empty). Those two getters read one word: FUN_02084BF8 is `*(0x0211A51C+4) in {1, 2}` and FUN_02084C4C is `*(0x0211A51C+4) == 2 && *(0x0211A51C+0xC) == -1`. So layout 4 is taken when the session word +4 is 1, or is 2 with +0xC not -1. 0x0211A51C is the multiplayer/quest SESSION object this repo already reaches through the same FUN_02084BF8 in data/enemy_difficulty_tier.json ('the table it guards is the multiplayer quest list') and through FUN_02084C78 in data/session_protocol.json. A single-player free field leaves +4 at 0, which is why the free-field sample never took this path. NOTE the bound: the +0x31 arm accepts 0..4, not 0..3, so a room record that somehow carried 4 would also take it -- the draw is what makes that unreachable, not the selector.
the_rule.4_where_plus31_comes_from: FUN_02082814 draws it at generation time: rand(100) against a 3x4 weight table at 0x020F2E70 selected by the room's tree depth -- depth<4 [50,20,20,10], depth 4..6 [40,20,20,20], depth>=7 [25,25,25,25]. So it is a RANDOM DRAW, not a function of the room.
the_rule.5_group_5_is_rolled: FUN_02030B6C seeds a private RNG from the room record's own seed at +0x14, draws rand(100) against [40,20,20,20] at 0x020EC270 for a count of 0..3, Fisher-Yates shuffles and takes that many. Groups 0..4 are built whole. objects_per_layout therefore EXCLUDES group 5.
the_rule.6_which_record_is_WHICH_OBJECT: the pair (factory index = record +0x14 low byte, variant = record +0x12) is looked up in the room's own stage registry object/<NN>/o<NN><v>_prm.rel, and when the stage registry has no such row, in the object/special/special_<tag>_prm.rel family. Factory index 3 is the container family: variant 0 = oNN_cont (box), 1 = oNN_wall, 2 = o0c_recont (rare box).
the_rule.caps: a group is truncated to 20 records and a room stops at 20 objects overall

treasure_box_rule._: THE RULE psz-godot NEEDS, stated plainly, because a game system is being built on it. THE TREASURE BOX IS NOT A BOSS REWARD AND IT IS NOT SPAWNED. Every o0c_trebox is an AUTHORED record in this file, placed at room load like everything else -- factory index 10's allocator 0x02080EEC has ZERO call sites in arm9 or any of the 32 overlays, and the factory table it sits in has exactly one word reference in the whole ROM. What the room-clear gates is the box's APPEARANCE.
treasure_box_rule.which_rooms: EVERY room that authors an o0c_trebox record, which is 1,306 of the 1,495 rooms in this file -- ordinary rooms and boss arenas alike. Not bosses only: all 25 boxes observed ACTIVE across the savestate corpus stand in ORDINARY rooms, over 13 distinct room codes, and 0 in a boss arena.
treasure_box_rule.when: WHEN THE ROOM IS CLEARED. The object exists from room load with its state byte +0x2E at 0 and its ACTIVE flag (bit 2 of +0x50) clear, and does nothing but poll FUN_0205136C(field map, current room, kind). That predicate requires bit `kind` of BYTE +6 of the field map's own 8-byte per-room record, and refuses for the room you are standing in while the map's live encounter object at map+0x64 is non-null. Bit 0 is set on the room the player is standing in at the moment its fight ends -- measured 65/65 across same-room before/after savestate pairs, one byte of the array moving and no other.
treasure_box_rule.kinds: The record's parameter block byte +9 is 0 or 1 and selects BOTH the permission bit and the drop table. Kind 0 is the ordinary room clear box. Kind 1 additionally requires FUN_02032E30 -- byte +0x32 of the room's 0x34-byte generated record must be >= 0 -- and is never observed active in this corpus.
treasure_box_rule.how_it_appears: Not a fade-in: it DROPS IN. On acceptance the object plays sound (0, 9), sets +0xB8 and runs FUN_02081900(obj, 1, 0, 0x1000); the update then walks its Y from +0xB8 down to the authored +0xBC and sets flag 8 on landing. State byte +0x2E: 0 waiting, 1 dropping in, 3 idle and openable, 5 opened.
treasure_box_rule.what_it_contains: n items, n = FUN_0209AF3C(kind) clamped to 20, each rolled by FUN_0209AEA4(kind, i, stack) out of a per-room content list the field map builds from its own cells. They are registered into THE SAME ground-item table as the breakable box -- 0x0211AAA4, insert FUN_0204F4A0, 16-byte item stacks -- so a port needs ONE ground-item system, not two. The difference is the roll: a breakable box registers ONE item and only after passing a d100 against its own record's percentage byte at parameter block +2, while the treasure box registers all n with no percentage roll.
treasure_box_rule.not_established: Which code writes byte +6 bit 0 is NOT located. The byte is read here and its transition is measured 65/65, but four THUMB scans over arm9 and all 32 overlays miss the store -- no ldrb/orr/strb at +6 on this array, no ldrh/strh pair, no strb [r,#6] preceded by an lsls #3 room index, no lsls #3 / adds #6. The scans are THUMB only and ov16 carries ARM bodies, so the writer may be a whole-record write, a register-offset store, or ARM code. The rule rests on the READER plus the measured transition. And no capture holds a boss arena AFTER the boss dies, so 'boss rooms follow the same rule' rests on the code path being identical, not on an observation.

volumes_rule._: The six factory indices that no registry names, and why no registry was ever going to. All six read variant 0xFF because none of them takes its subtype from the record -- each reads its own PARAMETER BLOCK -- so a (factory index, variant) row has nothing to say about them. The constructor the factory dispatches to does. Block layouts reconcile EXACTLY with the sizes the type ids declare.
volumes_rule.player_entry: factory index 1, type 0x0401, class 1, ctor FUN_02076E78, 52 bytes, no render node. THE PLAYER'S SPAWN POINT, not the warp trigger a3d7c7b recorded. block+0 is a s16 ENTRY ID; FUN_02032C3C(stage ctx, id) accepts it when *(ctx+0x20) == id, or when id == 0 and ctx+0x20 is negative -- a fresh arrival with no id. On acceptance the constructor copies the RECORD's own x/y/z and its u16 facing at +0x10 into (*0x02108C58)+0x28 through FUN_020403D0, which is SET-ONCE (`if p[4] == 0`), and separately -- unconditionally, whenever the id is 0 -- into +0x64..+0x74 of the same object through FUN_020405A8. That is why 36843ae measured index 1 at 0.01 cells from a doorway: you come in there.
volumes_rule.town_service: factory index 6, type 0x0806, class 5, ctor FUN_02076C60, 76 bytes. THE TOWN COUNTER. block+4, bounded 0 <= v < 10 by the constructor itself, indexes the byte table at 0x020F2870 into the game's own object-name table, and it is the ONE of only two types in the game that reaches the leaf name setter FUN_02076C58 (tools/objnames.py). block+0 is its interaction volume, installed through FUN_02044C08.
volumes_rule.mayors_office: factory index 9, type 0x0C09, class 8, ctor FUN_0207F9E8, 76 bytes. Its own constructor writes name index 31 -- `Mayor's Office` -- into the contextual box, on the same instruction pattern whose two independent anchors come out as `Card Key` (0x080D) and `Message Pack` (0x201C). One record in the whole corpus, in the City's `c` set.
volumes_rule.event_trigger_volume: factory index 27, type 0x281B, class 0x17, ctor FUN_020A05B4, 80 bytes, no render node and no model. A MODELLESS AUTHORED VOLUME. block+0 is a shape mode: 0 takes ONE dimension from block+4 (FUN_02076C4C builds {0, a, 0}), 1 takes TWO from block+8 and block+0xC (FUN_020A05A8 builds {1, a, b}); the descriptor goes to FUN_02044C08, the same call the town counter and the Mayor's Office use for their interaction volumes. Three event-flag conditions at block+0x10, +0x18 and +0x20; the +0x10 one is BROADCAST on message 0 by FUN_02030808 as message 7:2, which data/message_handlers.json resolves to FUN_0209CCC4.
volumes_rule.field_scene_effect: factory index 29, type 0x241D, class 0x14, ctor FUN_0209E424, 424 bytes, a flag-0x20 render node. block+0x20, bounded < 5, selects a scene/fse/<name>.narc through the RUNTIME table at 0x020FB624 -- see FSE_BY_SELECTOR in tools/objplace.py, and note it is a PERMUTATION of the static name table at 0x020FB604. block+0x21 is a 0..100 percent (FUN_0209A478 clamps it and divides by 100). Four conditions at block+0, +8, +0x10, +0x18. The two selectors the constructor singles out -- poison_0 and slow_0 -- take a branch that builds an attack packet through FUN_020926D0 with a constant of 0x17 and 0x18 respectively; what those two numbers ARE is not established here.
volumes_rule.ambient_sound: factory index 42, type 0x042A, class 0x24, ctor FUN_020AFFE0, 60 bytes, no render node. block+0 picks the constant its per-frame tick FUN_020B003C hands to FUN_02033690 -- 0 -> 9, 1 -> 15 -- and block+1 picks whether that call gets the emitter's own position (pan and volume derived from it) or the zero-vector sentinel at 0x020FC958 that FUN_02033690 reads as 'no position'. FUN_02033690 forwards to FUN_020C1D7C, a THREE-VOICE table at (*0x020C1E40)+0xC4.

declined_reasons.in_the_trap_dump: the record is one of the eight traps and is emitted, by name, in data/trap_placement_per_room.json. Declining it here is what stops a merged consumer double-placing it.
declined_reasons.unresolved_factory_index: the (factory index, variant) pair has no row in ANY of the 52 stage registries or the 13 special ones, so nothing in the ROM names a model for it. THIS REASON IS NOW EMPTY: the six indices that carried it are the six MODELLESS mechanisms and are emitted in `volumes`.
declined_reasons.parameter_block_too_short_to_decode: one of the six modelless indices whose parameter block is shorter than the fields its constructor reads, so the record is real but its parameters cannot be decoded. Also now empty.
declined_reasons.registry_row_with_no_model: the registry DOES carry the row and its model byte is 0xFF -- the object is real and invisible. Not a decode failure.
declined_reasons.stage_has_no_object_registry: the stage has no o<NN><v>_prm.rel at all (stage 00 variant e, the City), so there is nothing to resolve against.

modelless_factory_index._: the six indices no registry declares a model for. They are no longer DECLINED -- they are the `volumes` list, and the count here is the corpus census per index. The key was `unresolved_factory_index` up to a3d7c7b; nothing about the counts changed, only what is done with them.

NOT_ESTABLISHED: RETRACTED, and it was MY OWN reading: index 1 is NOT the invisible warp trigger. a3d7c7b and 25ca38f both recorded it that way, on the strength of 'index 1 or 4 predicts warp-model residency 68/68' -- which is true, and which does not distinguish a warp from the spawn point a warp lands you on. Its constructor places the PLAYER. See volumes_rule.player_entry. What survives from 25ca38f untouched: the warp MODELS belong to factory index 4, and no registry names a model for index 1.

WHAT `strength_percent` MEANS on field_scene_effect is not established. FUN_0209A478 clamps block+0x21 to 0..100 and computes v/100 as a 1.19.12 fraction, so it IS a percentage of something; the corpus authors 1 (126), 5 (17) and 2 (6). Which quantity it scales was not traced.

THE TWO CONSTANTS 0x17 AND 0x18 that field_scene_effect's poison_0 and slow_0 branches put into their attack packet are NOT status-effect ids. data/status_effects.json establishes the status index space as exactly SIX wide, so 23 and 24 are out of it. They are recorded as measured values and not named.

SELECTORS 2 (slow_0) AND 4 (the second shadow_0 pointer) of field_scene_effect: 4 is authored by NO record in the corpus, so the permutation's last entry is asserted from FUN_020EB748's stores alone and never from data.
WHAT THE AMBIENT SOUND CONSTANTS 9 AND 15 NAME is not established -- they are the two arguments FUN_02033690 forwards, and no sound-id table was located. The mechanism is; the sounds are not.

WHICH SPECIAL TAG A ROOM LOADS is still untraced (fmt.room-object-set open question). It does not block naming -- every special archive that declares a given (index, variant) declares the SAME model -- but it does mean this dump cannot say which archive a room's warp model comes from.

FACTORY INDEX 40 (o0c_needle, o0c_poisonm, 382 records) IS EMITTED and is NOT a trap: 23ddc66 scored it as the adversarial lookalike and it names itself nothing at two levels of call depth. The model is a fact; the behaviour is not established.

o0c_trebox IS THE TREASURE BOX and the open question is closed, but the reason matters: NOT because `trebox` looks like `treasure box`. Factory index 10 is type 0x0C0A, whose constructor FUN_02080F04 writes name index 4 into the contextual info box, and index 4 of object/text/object_text_info_window.bin is the literal string `Treasure Box`. That scan's two controls are types whose identity was fixed from behaviour long before it -- 0x080D comes out `Card Key` and 0x201C `Message Pack` -- and the rival reading (the small literal each constructor passes to FUN_02076574) makes 0x080D `Switch` and 0x201C `Weapon Shop`. The stem and the name AGREE, and the agreement is earned rather than assumed. Its BEHAVIOUR is still open: class 9, 192 bytes, six states, and 23ddc66's residency oddity (resident in 68 of 68 room images while only 44 author one) is unexplained.
